valuation_philosophy: Kingfish is a closed-end listed investment company (LIC) on the NZX, managed by Fisher Funds, holding a concentrated portfolio of quality NZ companies (F&P Healthcare ~19%, Infratil ~17%, Mainfreight ~8%, Summerset ~8%, Auckland Airport ~8%). It has NO operating revenue, NO EBITDA, and reported 'Revenue'/NetIncome in the Metrics.csv are total investment income including mark-to-market swings (negative in FY2022/23/26) -- an FCF/WACC/Gordon-growth DCF is structurally inapplicable, exactly as for the other LICs in this research folder (BIT.NZ, AFI.NZ, BIF.NZ). This model instead uses NAV-per-share compounding x exit price-to-NAV, discounted at cost of equity: (a) split the portfolio's total return into fees, the cash distribution, and the residual change in NAV per share, then compound NAV/share forward; (b) apply a scenario exit P/NAV multiple to the year-5 NAV; (c) intrinsic value = PV(5 years of dividends per share) + PV(year-5 NAV/share x exit P/NAV), discounted at cost of equity. CRITICAL POINT: the ~8-9% headline dividend yield is NOT free income stacked on top of NAV growth -- it is funded first from the portfolio's own total return, and only the RESIDUAL after fees and the fixed 8%-of-NAV distribution shows up as NAV growth (which, on realistic assumptions, is negative). This is not a modelling assumption; it already happened -- statutory NAV/share fell from $1.57 (FY2019) to $1.20 (FY2026), a -3.8%/yr CAGR, even as total net assets grew, because 358.8m shares (vs 197.9m in FY2019, +81%) were issued via warrants and a 3%-discounted DRP. FY2026 alone paid $38.1m of dividends against only $10.5m of dividend/interest income and a $13.6m net LOSS -- the distribution is substantially return of capital, mechanically eroding NAV/share. Kingfish also currently trades at only a ~1% discount to NAV (vs a 5-6.5% discount in FY2023-25 and an 11.6% PREMIUM in FY2022) -- unlike most LICs in this book there is no discount-closing catalyst available to a new buyer; the buyer pays close to full NAV for a portfolio of NZ blue chips plus a ~1.1% annual fee load (management fee 0.75-1.25% of adjusted NAV, floating with performance, plus a 10% performance fee above a bank-bill+7% hurdle) that a passive NZX50 index fund would avoid almost entirely. The honest framing: Kingfish is an income-distribution vehicle suited to investors who want NZ blue-chip equity exposure plus a steady (if capital-eroding) quarterly cash stream, not a compounding growth investment. If the base case below is negative against the $1.20 market price, that is the model's genuine conclusion, not an input error -- it is reported as such rather than adjusted to manufacture upside.
wacc_rationale: Cost of equity is built up as NZ risk-free rate (~4.5%, 10yr NZGB) + equity risk premium (~6.0%) for a diversified large/mid-cap NZ equity portfolio, which nets to roughly 10.5% unlevered. Kingfish itself carries ZERO debt (net assets ARE the NAV, no leveraged-beta adjustment needed) so no leverage uplift applies. A small downward adjustment versus a raw 10.5% is justified because the underlying portfolio (F&P Healthcare, Infratil, Mainfreight, Summerset, Auckland Airport) is blue-chip/large-cap, not small-cap -- so no large small-cap illiquidity premium is layered on. A small offsetting premium is added for the structural agency/fee drag and the closed-end wrapper's own (thinner) NZX liquidity versus its constituents. Net: base case cost of equity 10.0%, bull 9.5% (manager outperformance reduces perceived agency risk), bear 10.5% (persistent underperformance/fee drag raises the required return). The SAME rate is used consistently to discount both dividends and the exit value, and is exposed in the standard `wacc` assumption field so dashboard sliders operate on it directly.

inputs.shares_note: 358,844,193 shares on issue at 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 year end) is used as the base for the projection. A further 1,218,425 shares were issued 6-May-2026 from the 1.40% take-up of the KFLWI warrant exercise (the remaining 85.7m warrants lapsed), taking the count to ~360.06m -- a <0.4% difference, immaterial to per-share NAV projections and not separately modelled.
inputs.nav_per_share_note: FY2026 statutory (as-reported) NAV per share at 31-Mar-2026, used as the conservative projection anchor. The most recent weekly disclosure (29-Jul-2026) showed an undiluted NAV of $1.2977, ~8% higher, reflecting the post-year-end market recovery; using the lower statutory figure is the conservative choice and is directly comparable to the audited net-assets figure below.
inputs.net_debt_note: Kingfish carries ZERO borrowings by mandate -- net assets ARE the NAV. Net debt is NOT subtracted anywhere in this model (unlike an operating-company DCF); NAV per share already nets everything.
inputs.fcf_not_applicable_note: Free cash flow is not a meaningful concept for a closed-end investment company -- operating cash flow reflects portfolio buying/selling, not earnings, and there is no capex/working-capital cycle. The economically equivalent basis used throughout this model is dividend/interest income received (FY2026: $10.5m, or ~2.9cps) versus the $38.1m ($10.84cps) actually distributed -- the gap is return of capital. This income figure is NOT used as a DCF base; see valuation_philosophy.
inputs.sbc_source: not applicable -- Kingfish is an externally-managed LIC (Fisher Funds) with no employees and no share-based compensation scheme
inputs.buyback_cash_note: 0.7m shares repurchased in FY2026 (FY2025: 4.8m) at a market price close to $1.19-1.28, approx $0.9m cash outflow; used tactically when the discount to NAV widens, authority capped at 5% of shares on issue. Not material enough to change the projected share count and is not separately modelled as an offset -- buybacks below NAV are mildly NAV-accretive and are implicitly folded into the fee-drag/net-return assumption rather than modelled as a discrete mechanic.
inputs.projected_shares_note: Held flat for projection purposes. Warrant/DRP dilution is a real historical driver of the NAV/share CAGR (shares +81% since FY2019) but is not separately re-modelled forward since there is no current warrant series outstanding after the May-2026 KFLWI lapse; NAV/share growth is instead calculated directly (net return minus distribution) which already captures the economics of any future issuance below NAV as a further drag not explicitly quantified here.
inputs.dividend_policy: 2.0% of average NAV paid EACH QUARTER (~8% annualised); next dividend 2.49cps payable 26-Jun-2026

historical_growth.fy2026_gross_return_vs_benchmark: gross performance return -2.1% vs S&P/NZX50G +5.2%, underperformance of 7.3pp
historical_growth.revenue_not_meaningful_note: The 'Revenue' column in the Metrics.csv is total investment income including realised/unrealised mark-to-market portfolio movements and is negative in FY2022 (-10.654), FY2023 (-14.671) and FY2026 (-8.303) -- a CAGR over a series that changes sign is not computable/meaningful and is left null.
historical_growth.eps_not_meaningful_note: EPS is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings (FY2021 EPS 56.28c vs FY2022 -5.49c on a similar share base) and is not a proxy for a repeatable operating trend.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: Net assets (equity) grew over 7 years despite falling NAV/share purely because shares on issue rose 81% (197.9m to 358.8m) via warrant exercises and a discounted DRP; net assets have actually SHRUNK over the last 3 and 5 years (FY2026 $431.4m vs FY2021 $551.4m) as the FY2022-23 and FY2026 losses combined with the uncovered distribution outpaced new issuance.
historical_growth.fcf_not_meaningful_note: See inputs.fcf_not_applicable_note -- no FCF concept applies to a closed-end fund.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (net assets) CAGR (+4.8% 7yr) diverges sharply from NAV-per-share CAGR (-3.8% 7yr) -- a textbook LIC dilution pattern, not a data error. Net asset growth is entirely a function of gross share issuance (warrants struck near/below NAV, DRP at a 3% discount) outrunning the NAV-per-share decline; it says nothing about whether existing shareholders are being made better or worse off. NAV-per-share is used as the growth driver for this reason, consistent with the equivalent treatment for BIT.NZ/AFI.NZ/BIF.NZ in this research folder.
historical_growth.notes: The defining historical fact for KFL.NZ is that NAV per share has fallen at a -3.8%/yr CAGR over 7 years (-7.5%/yr over the most recent 5) while total net assets rose, entirely due to a distribution policy (~8%/yr of NAV) that is structurally uncovered by the portfolio's actual total return in most years, funded by ongoing share issuance below/near NAV. The 5-year adjusted-NAV-return of only +0.5% p.a. (vs benchmark +0.6% p.a.) shows the manager has barely broken even net of fees over the period, even before the distribution policy's mechanical erosion of NAV/share is layered on.

base.rationale: Gross return of 6.5%/yr approximates a long-run NZX50G-type total return for a diversified blue-chip NZ portfolio, roughly consistent with Kingfish's own 5yr benchmark annualised return of 0.6% blended toward a more normal long-run NZ equity return assumption (the trailing 5yr figure is depressed by two down years, FY2022 and FY2026, that should not simply be extrapolated). Fee drag of 1.1% matches the FY2026 OPEX ratio. Net return of 5.4% against an 8%-of-NAV distribution policy implies NAV/share DECLINES ~2.6%/yr -- materially less severe than the realised 7yr CAGR (-3.8%) because the FY2019-2026 period included two sharp drawdowns (FY2020 COVID, FY2022-23 rate shock) this projection does not assume repeat. Exit P/NAV of 0.95 is the mid of the 5yr historical discount range (0.93-1.12x, ex the FY2022 premium outlier), i.e. a modest reversion from today's near-par 0.99x back toward the more typical discount regime.

bull.rationale: Manager adds genuine alpha and NZ small/mid caps re-rate from currently subdued levels (Chair explicitly frames current valuations as attractive entry points for 'patient, long-term investors'); portfolio names with disclosed multi-year growth plans (Mercury underlying earnings +30% over 5yr, Contact EBITDAF to $1.2-1.3bn, Infratil's CDC AI-driven data-centre demand) deliver. Fee drag is modelled HIGHER (1.15% vs 1.1% base), not lower, because strong performance re-engages the 10% performance fee above the bank-bill+7% hurdle (currently dormant, high-water mark $1.15) -- reflecting the mechanical fee structure honestly rather than assuming fees fall in the good case. Net return of 8.35% against the fixed 8% distribution leaves NAV/share roughly FLAT (+0.35%/yr), i.e. the distribution becomes approximately covered rather than reversed. Exit P/NAV of 1.00 assumes the fund continues to trade at par, as it does today.

bear.rationale: NZ market stagnates (consistent with the FY2026 pattern of NZX50G volatility around geopolitical/oil shocks and a manager that has now underperformed its benchmark by 7.3pp in the latest year), and the manager continues to lag as concentrated single-name risk (top 5 = ~60% of the portfolio; FY2026 was hurt by Vista -55%, EBOS -39%, Vulcan Steel -27%, Summerset -19%) repeats. Fee drag rises slightly (1.2%) as the automatic rebate mechanism only partially offsets a mediocre-but-not-catastrophic result. Against a fixed 8% distribution, net return of only 1.8% implies NAV/share erodes ~6.2%/yr -- close to the realised 5yr CAGR of -7.5%. Exit P/NAV of 0.90 assumes the discount re-widens beyond the FY2024 level (6.5%) as investor patience with a persistently underperforming, uncovered-distribution vehicle wanes.

base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a -- LIC valuation uses P/NAV, not an earnings multiple; exit P/NAV = 0.95
base.note: intrinsic_value = PV(5yr dividends) + PV(year-5 NAV/share x exit P/NAV), both discounted at 10.0% cost of equity. No 'net debt' subtraction (Kingfish has none) and no separate enterprise/equity value split -- NAV per share already nets everything.

entry_price.methodology: Price today at which buying now, collecting base-case projected dividends per share for 5 years, and exiting at year-5 NAV/share x base-case exit P/NAV (0.95) earns a 15% IRR. Uses the base-case dividend/NAV path (the decelerating actual projection, not a constant growth proxy), discounted at 15% rather than the 10.0% cost of equity. Because Kingfish's realistic total return (~5.4% net of fees, against an 8%-of-NAV payout that erodes NAV/share ~2.6%/yr) is far below a 15% hurdle, the entry price implied is well below both intrinsic value and the current market price -- this is the correct, expected output for a fund earning single-digit total returns, not a modelling error.

sensitivity.methodology: Base-case NAV/dividend path (gross return 6.5%, fee drag 1.1%, distribution 8% of NAV -> NAV/share declining 2.6%/yr) held constant; each cell varies only the discount rate (row) and the year-5 exit price-to-NAV multiple (column). NOTE: for a closed-end fund the second sensitivity axis is exit P/NAV, not 'terminal growth' -- there is no Gordon-growth terminal value in this model.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weighted above the standard 25% because the central dynamic (a distribution policy exceeding realistic total return, mechanically eroding NAV/share) is not a hypothetical risk but the pattern actually observed over 7 of the last 8 years (NAV/share fell in 6 of 8 years shown). Bull is held at only 25% because it requires BOTH a return to genuine manager outperformance (reversing the FY2026 -7.3pp benchmark miss) AND the discount to stay at today's unusually tight ~1% level.

sanity_check.applicable_multiples_note: Standard P/E and EV/EBITDA gates are NOT APPLICABLE to a closed-end investment company -- NetIncome/EPS is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings (not a repeatable earnings stream) and there is no EBITDA concept (no operating business, no revenue, no cost base to derive it from). Both are recorded as null below. The meaningful multiple for a LIC is PRICE-TO-NAV, which is used instead.
sanity_check.diagnosis: PASS. Base-case implied P/NAV of 0.806x sits comfortably BELOW the entire 5-year historical range (0.935x-1.116x), let alone the 1.674x trip threshold -- the model is not assuming any unrealistic re-rating. If anything the base case implies the market SHOULD price Kingfish at a wider discount than the ~1% it currently trades at (current_price / nav0 = 1.20/1.20 = 1.0), which is the honest, expected direction of the result given the NAV-erosion dynamic documented in valuation_philosophy. Standard P/E and EV/EBITDA checks were skipped as structurally inapplicable to a closed-end fund with no operating earnings base -- this is a schema-consistency null, not a missing data point.
sanity_check.direction_of_conclusion: The model finds Kingfish roughly FAIRLY-TO-SLIGHTLY-OVER priced at $1.20 (base case -19.4%, weighted -19.9%), consistent with the current ~1% discount to NAV being unusually tight versus the 5yr average ~5% discount, and consistent with the qualitative bear case (uncovered distribution policy, persistent benchmark underperformance, high fee load versus passive alternatives).
